questions.question: When stopped on the side of the road, what should the driver do?

options.text: Keep their side door open.
Turn on their emergency flashers.
Wave their arms.
Turn off all their lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on their emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers. This warns other drivers about your stopped vehicle.

questions.question: What should you know about people working on a disabled vehicle?

options.text: They are probably aware of the roadway.
They may be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.
They are not subject to traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people repairing a vehicle on the road. They may be focused on their work and not paying attention to traffic nearby.

questions.question: How much alcohol can a liver process per hour?

options.text: One drink
Two drinks
Three drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: One drink
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol from your body at a fixed rate of about one drink per hour. Drinking faster than this will increase your blood alcohol content.

questions.question: When does hydroplaning happen most often?

options.text: When a vehicle is traveling faster than 60 mph.
When tire pressure is too low.
When tire tread is too deep.

questions.correctAnswerText: When tire pressure is too low.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is most likely when driving on wet roads with low tire pressure and worn tires. Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: What should you do when backing a truck?

options.text: Rely on your mirrors to guide you.
First walk around the area to check for obstacles.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: First walk around the area to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing a truck, walk around to check for obstacles in your path. Mirrors have blind spots, so you cannot rely on them alone. Use a helper if possible.

questions.question: After cargo is secured, how often should you check it?

options.text: You do not need to check it again for the entire trip.
You can drive at least eight hours without checking it.
Every three hours or 150 miles.
You should not check it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every three hours or 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: When checking air and electrical lines, which is NOT acceptable?

options.text: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
The air hoses and electrical lines are not cut.
The air lines are not pinched.
The air lines are not dragging against tractor parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
questions.explanation: During inspection, listen for leaks in the air hoses. Check that hoses and lines are not cut, worn, tangled, pinched, or dragging against parts of the vehicle.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With both hands.
With one hand to allow eating and drinking.
With one hand at a time, switching between hands.
With a cracked grip for better control.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands. Place your hands on opposite sides of the wheel to maintain proper control.

questions.question: If Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working on a truck, what happens?

options.text: The truck will have no brakes.
The truck should only be driven at low speeds.
The truck will still have brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: ABS is an extra system that prevents brakes from locking up during hard braking. If ABS stops working, your regular brakes will still work. You can continue to drive and brake normally.

questions.question: How should parts of an exhaust system be?

options.text: Loose.
Leaking.
Fastened securely.
Cracked.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Exhaust system parts must be securely mounted and not loose, broken, or missing. The system should not rub against moving parts of the vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when fueling a bus with passengers on board?

options.text: Do it often during long trips.
Only do it if absolutely necessary.
It is fine as long as passengers stay inside the bus.
Do it to show passengers there is enough fuel to reach the next stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only do it if absolutely necessary.
questions.explanation: Do not refuel a bus while passengers are on board unless absolutely necessary. Never refuel a bus with passengers inside an enclosed building.

questions.question: When checking tires, which finding is NOT a problem?

options.text: Too much air pressure
Front tire tread of at least 4/32 of an inch deep in the grooves
Radial and bias-ply tires mixed together

questions.correctAnswerText: Front tire tread of at least 4/32 of an inch deep in the grooves
questions.explanation: Check that tire air pressure is not too low or too high. Check that front tires have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth in every groove. Do not mix radial and bias-ply tires together.

questions.question: After a crash, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Protect the accident area.
Call the police or proper authorities.
Help any injured people.
Drive away without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive away without stopping.
questions.explanation: After a crash, you must protect the accident area, call the proper authorities, and help injured people. Protecting the area right away helps prevent another crash at the same spot.

questions.question: What is aggressive driving?

options.text: Driving in a selfish or pushy way without regard for others
Driving with some concern for other drivers' safety
Driving in the left lane
Driving a loud vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in a selfish or pushy way without regard for others
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving means operating a vehicle in a selfish, bold, or pushy way without concern for the rights or safety of other people.

questions.question: When pulling back into traffic after stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Assume other drivers will let you merge.
Wait for a large enough gap to accelerate and merge safely.
Have a passenger get out and direct traffic for you.
Honk your horn until other drivers let you merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large enough gap to accelerate and merge safely.
questions.explanation: Know how fast your bus accelerates and how much space it needs on the road. Always wait for a gap in traffic large enough for your vehicle before leaving a stop.

questions.question: When construction workers are near the road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Avoid all lanes.
Wait until construction is finished before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Follow the posted speed limit in construction zones. Slow down even more when workers are close to the road.

questions.question: During the road test, which is an example of poor lane usage?

options.text: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks
Stopping behind crosswalks
Using the leftmost lane when more lanes are available
Finishing a right turn in the rightmost lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Using the leftmost lane when more lanes are available
questions.explanation: During the road test, do not drive over curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings. Stop behind stop lines, crosswalks, and stop signs. On roads with multiple lanes, finish turns in the correct lane. Always stay in or move to the rightmost lane unless it is blocked.

questions.question: If a speed limit is posted, what does this mean?

options.text: Never exceed the posted speed.
You can exceed it when passing another vehicle.
You can exceed it in rural areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never exceed the posted speed.
questions.explanation: A posted speed limit is the fastest you may drive under perfect conditions. Slow down as road and weather conditions require. Never drive faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: During a pre-trip check, what should you look for on power steering hoses?

options.text: Leaks
Secure connections to the battery
Extra hose pieces for repairs

questions.correctAnswerText: Leaks
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip check on a vehicle with power steering, inspect the hoses, pump, and fluid level. Check the hoses carefully for any leaks.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts hydroplaning, what should you do?

options.text: Press the accelerator.
Do not use the brakes.
Shift to a higher gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not brake. Instead, slow down by releasing the accelerator and pressing in the clutch.
